title: Sunny and the Dragonfly | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka watches a dragonfly rest its delicate wings on a reed at dusk, its wings catching the last golden light like tiny stained glass windows. A peaceful bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
The dragonfly had been flying all day.

Sunny saw her land — right there on a tall reed beside the creek — just as the last gold light was fading from the sky.

She was extraordinary. Her wings were so thin they were nearly invisible, but when the light caught them, they lit up like tiny windows of colour — amber, blue, green — all at once.

Her body was a thread of brilliant turquoise.

She held perfectly still.

Sunny held perfectly still too.

They watched each other. The dragonfly's huge eyes were dark and round and seemed to take in the whole world at once — the water, the reeds, the last of the sunset, Sunny herself.

Slowly the light changed from gold to soft rose to the first pale purple of evening.

The dragonfly's wings moved — just once, a tiny flicker — and then stilled again.

A little star appeared. Then another.

Sunny looked at the dragonfly. She thought: you have been so busy all day. Flying and turning and catching light. Now it is time to rest.

The dragonfly seemed to agree. She settled more deeply onto the reed, her wings folded flat.

Sunny settled too. She curled up in the soft grass at the creek's edge.

The stars were coming out now, one by one.

The creek whispered.

And both of them rested.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, dragonfly. Goodnight, little one.
